## A library, in one picture {#library}

```
5'-[P5][i5][Read 1 primer]=====cDNA insert=====[Read 2 primer][i7][P7]-3'
```

- **P5 / P7**: stick to the flow cell
- **i5 / i7 index**: your sample's barcode
- **Insert**: your RNA (as cDNA), ~150–400 bp

## Paired-end sequencing {#paired-end}

```
insert:  5'-ACGTTGCA..............................GGATCCTA-3'
Read 1:     ACGTTGCA.......>
Read 2:                               <.......TAGGATCC
```

- `2x100` = 100 bases from each end
- **Depth**: read pairs per sample (20–30 M for gene-level DE)
- Insert shorter than the read → read runs into **adapter** → trimming

## Demultiplexing {#demultiplexing}

The core sorts reads by **index** into files per sample:

```
WT_Treated_Rep1_S4_R1_001.fastq.gz
└ sample name ─┘└S#┘└R1┘└001┘
```

- Two samples with the same index → **mixed forever**
- Several lanes (`_L001_`, `_L002_`) → join them before analysis

## Strandedness (dUTP) {#strandedness}

Most stranded kits (TruSeq Stranded, NEB Directional):

- **Read 1** = reverse complement of the RNA (antisense)
- **Read 2** = same as the RNA (sense)

A gene on the **+** strand → Read 1 aligns to **−**.

Ask the core: **which kit? stranded?**

## Where to run it {#computing}

| | Laptop | Workstation | Cluster |
|---|---|---|---|
| For | learning, R | one project | many samples, pipelines |
| RAM | 8–32 GB | 64–256 GB | lots per node |
| Run tools by | typing | typing | **jobs** |
| Software | conda | conda | conda or **modules** |

Windows → install **WSL** first.

## Clusters in one picture {#cluster}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart LR
  L["laptop"] -- ssh --> LN["login node<br/>light work only"]
  LN -- "sbatch / srun" --> S["SLURM"]
  S --> C1["compute"] & C2["compute"]
  C1 & C2 --- FS[("home · scratch · project")]
```

- **Never** run heavy tools on the login node
- **Scratch**: big, fast, purged. **Project**: kept.

## SLURM in five commands {#slurm}

```bash
srun -c 4 --mem=8g -t 2:00:00 --pty bash    # interactive job
sbatch my_job.sh                            # batch job
squeue -u $USER                             # what's running
sacct -j 123456                             # how did it go
scancel 123456                              # stop it
```

## Software: conda {#conda}

```bash
conda env create -f envs/rnaseq-tools.yml   # once
conda activate rnaseq-tools                 # every new terminal
salmon --version
```

Apple Silicon error? `CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 conda env create ...`

## The shell {#shell}

```bash
ls   -l   -h   ~/omics-walkthru-practice
#^   ^^^^^^^   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#program options  argument
```

- **Absolute** path: starts with `/`
- **Relative** path: from where you are (`pwd`)
- `.` here · `..` up one · `~` home · **Tab** autocompletes

## Plain text vs binary {#plain-text}

| Plain text (read with `less`) | Binary (need a tool) |
|---|---|
| FASTQ, FASTA, GTF, BED, SAM, samplesheet | BAM, bigWig, RDS |

Tables are **tab-separated**. Check tabs: `cat -A file | head` (tabs = `^I`).

## gzip {#gzip}

```bash
zcat reads.fastq.gz | head -8        # look without unpacking (macOS: gzip -dc)
gzip -t reads.fastq.gz && echo OK    # is it complete?
md5sum reads.fastq.gz                # fingerprint
```

- FASTQ compresses 3–5×
- Tools read `.gz` directly: **don't unzip**

## stdout, stderr, redirection {#redirection}

```bash
tool ... > out.txt                  # results to a file
tool ... 1> log.out 2> log.err      # results and messages apart
```

Many tools write their summary to **stderr** → check the `.err` file.

## Pipes {#pipes}

```bash
zcat reads.fastq.gz | head -4000 | wc -l
hisat2 ... | samtools view -u | samtools sort -o out.bam
```

Small tools, joined. No files in between.

## Try it {#try-it}

::: {.try}
```bash
source ~/omics-walkthru-practice/env.sh; conda activate rnaseq-tools
ls $DATA
zcat $DATA/N61311_untrt_R1_001.fastq.gz | head -8
for f in $DATA/*_R1_001.fastq.gz; do echo "$(basename $f): $(( $(gzip -dc $f | wc -l) / 4 ))"; done
```
:::

How many reads per file? Why divide by 4?

## Recap {#recap}

- Libraries → paired reads → demultiplexed FASTQ
- Know your **kit** and **strandedness**
- Laptop, workstation or cluster: same commands
- Shell: paths, plain text, gzip, pipes
